scope: Primary abstracts and results were read. Published findings are evidence for related methods; every Elpis starter remains unproven until measured locally.

least-to-most.title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
least-to-most.authors: Denny Zhou; Nathanael Schärli; Le Hou; Jason Wei; Nathan Scales; Xuezhi Wang; Dale Schuurmans; Claire Cui; Olivier Bousquet; Quoc Le; Ed Chi
least-to-most.finding: SCAN length-split accuracy: code-davinci-002, 16.2% chain-of-thought → 99.7% least-to-most (Table 8).

plan-solve.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
plan-solve.authors: Lei Wang; Wanyu Xu; Yihuai Lan; Zhiqiang Hu; Yunshi Lan; Roy Ka-Wei Lee; Ee-Peng Lim
plan-solve.finding: GSM8K accuracy with text-davinci-003: 56.4% zero-shot CoT → 59.3% PS+ (Table 2).

self-refine.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
self-refine.authors: Aman Madaan; Niket Tandon; Prakhar Gupta; Skyler Hallinan; Luyu Gao; Sarah Wiegreffe; Uri Alon; Nouha Dziri; Shrimai Prabhumoye; Yiming Yang; Shashank Gupta; Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder; Katherine Hermann; Sean Welleck; Amir Yazdanbakhsh; Peter Clark
self-refine.finding: GPT-4 code optimization: programs optimized, 27.3% → 36.0%; math solve rate barely changes, 92.9% → 93.1% (Table 1).

self-consistency.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
self-consistency.authors: Xuezhi Wang; Jason Wei; Dale Schuurmans; Quoc Le; Ed H. Chi; Sharan Narang; Aakanksha Chowdhery; Denny Zhou
self-consistency.finding: PaLM-540B GSM8K accuracy: 56.5% greedy CoT → 74.4% self-consistency with 40 sampled paths (Table 2).

metagpt.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
metagpt.authors: Sirui Hong; Mingchen Zhuge; Jiaqi Chen; Xiawu Zheng; Yuheng Cheng; Ceyao Zhang; Jinlin Wang; Zili Wang; Steven Ka Shing Yau; Zijuan Lin; Liyang Zhou; Chenyu Ran; Lingfeng Xiao; Chenglin Wu; Jürgen Schmidhuber
metagpt.finding: GPT-4 MetaGPT reports HumanEval pass@1 85.9% and MBPP 87.7% (Section 4.1); this is a bundled system result, not a topology ablation.

debate.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
debate.authors: Yilun Du; Shuang Li; Antonio Torralba; Joshua B. Tenenbaum; Igor Mordatch
debate.finding: ChatGPT GSM8K accuracy on 100 problems: single agent 77.0 ± 4.2% → debate 85.0 ± 3.5%, using 3 agents and 2 rounds (Table 1).

mindsearch.title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
mindsearch.authors: Zehui Chen; Kuikun Liu; Qiuchen Wang; Jiangning Liu; Wenwei Zhang; Kai Chen; Feng Zhao
mindsearch.finding: GPT-4o closed-set QA average score: ReAct Search 55.1 → MindSearch 59.8 (Table 1). Open-set analysis says factuality did not improve (Section 3.1.2).

patterns.name: Split by parts
patterns.proven: Structured multi-agent software workflows have measured benchmark results.
patterns.unproven: No direct evidence found for this exact three independent writers plus join graph. MetaGPT uses roles and shared SOPs, not this split; Elpis speed, quality and token benefit are unproven.

patterns.name: Sequential (prompt chaining)
patterns.proven: Sequential subproblem solving improves SCAN in the cited model and prompting setup.
patterns.unproven: Three separate writing agents with file handoffs are not validated by this single-model prompting study; its gains do not transfer automatically.

patterns.name: Plan → Build
patterns.proven: Planning before solving improves the cited arithmetic accuracy.
patterns.unproven: A planner followed by two parallel builders is not validated by Plan-and-Solve; it tests a prompt strategy, not separate coding agents.

patterns.name: Evaluator–optimizer
patterns.proven: Feedback followed by revision can improve code optimization; the paper also reports negligible math gains.
patterns.unproven: Elpis’s draft/check/improve graph is not validated by this paper. Its checks and one revision differ from iterative Self-Refine; model feedback is not ground truth.

patterns.name: Voting
patterns.proven: Sampling diverse answers and aggregating improves the cited GSM8K benchmark.
patterns.unproven: Three file-writing voters plus a model tally are not validated here; the paper marginalizes 40 sampled paths. Correlated errors, ties and a mistaken tally remain possible.

patterns.name: Hierarchical (orchestrator and teams)
patterns.proven: MetaGPT measures a complete structured multi-agent coding system.
patterns.unproven: No direct evidence found for this fixed lead/two team leads/four workers/join tree. The reported result does not isolate hierarchy or establish Elpis gains.

patterns.name: Debate + judge
patterns.proven: Multiple rounds of critique improve GSM8K in the cited small sample.
patterns.unproven: Two independent cases plus a judge are not validated by this paper: Elpis has no rebuttal rounds, and the study uses three debating agents.

patterns.name: Multi-agent research
patterns.proven: A planner and parallel searchers improve the cited closed-set QA aggregate.
patterns.unproven: This fixed four-researcher/report/citation-check graph is not validated. MindSearch dynamically expands its graph; Anthropic’s vendor research result is not an independent paper validating this starter.

patterns.name: Deep research
patterns.proven: Planner/searcher decomposition has related measured QA evidence.
patterns.unproven: No direct evidence found for this exact scope/supervisor/three researchers/report graph. LangGraph’s Open Deep Research is an implementation source, not proof of this Elpis starter.

patterns.name: Blank playground
patterns.proven: No efficacy claim: this is an empty editor.
patterns.unproven: No direct evidence exists for an unspecified user graph; every custom topology needs its own comparison.
